content: Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine that is commonly used to alleviate symptoms associated with allergies, hay fever, and the common cold. These symptoms include rash, itching, watery eyes, itchy eyes/nose/throat, cough, runny nose, and sneezing. Additionally, it is utilized to prevent and treat nausea, vomiting, and dizziness caused by motion sickness. The medication functions by blocking histamine, a natural substance produced by the body during an allergic reaction. Cough-and-cold products containing diphenhydramine have not been proven safe or effective for children under 6 years of age. Therefore, these products should not be used to treat cold symptoms in children younger than 6 unless explicitly directed by a doctor. Certain formulations, such as long-acting tablets or capsules, are not recommended for children under 12 years of age. These products do not cure or shorten the duration of the common cold and may lead to serious side effects. To minimize the risk of adverse effects, it is essential to follow all dosage instructions carefully. This medication should not be used to induce sleep in children. Avoid administering other cough-and-cold medications that may contain the same or similar ingredients. When using diphenhydramine, follow the instructions provided on the product packaging or as directed by your doctor. The medication can be taken in tablet, capsule, or liquid form, with or without food. If using the liquid form, measure the dose with a special measuring device or spoon to ensure accuracy; household spoons are not recommended. Rapidly-dissolving tablets or strips should be allowed to dissolve on the tongue before swallowing, with or without water. The dosage is determined based on factors such as age, medical condition, and response to treatment. Since there are various brands and formulations of diphenhydramine, it is important to read the dosing instructions for each product carefully, as the amount of diphenhydramine may vary. To prevent motion sickness, take the medication 30 minutes before engaging in activities such as travel. For sleep aid purposes, take the dose approximately 30 minutes before bedtime. Common side effects of diphenhydramine include drowsiness, dizziness, constipation, stomach upset, blurred vision, and dryness of the mouth, nose, or throat. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. If you experience any concerning symptoms, contact your doctor for medical advice. In the United States, you can also report side effects to the FDA, and in Canada, to Health Canada. Before taking diphenhydramine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to dimenhydrinate, or to any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Diphenhydramine may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. Certain liquid products, chewable tablets, or dissolving tablets/strips may contain sugar and/or aspartame. Liquid products may also contain alcohol. Exercise caution if you have diabetes, liver disease, phenylketonuria (PKU), or any other condition that necessitates limiting or avoiding these substances in your diet. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug, and older adults may be particularly susceptible to drowsiness, dizziness, confusion, constipation, or difficulty urinating. During pregnancy, diphenhydramine should only be used when clearly necessary. This drug passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Consult your doctor before using this medication while breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of diphenhydramine or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels of all your medications, such as allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. Diphenhydramine may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as allergy skin tests, potentially leading to false results. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Symptoms of overdose may include severe drowsiness, seizures, or widened pupils. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store diphenhydramine at room temperature, away from moisture and light. Do not store it in the bathroom, and do not freeze liquid forms of the medication. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about diphenhydramine. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
